## Question

The Long-Term Evolution Experiment provides genome sequences from *Escherichia coli* sampled over 50,000 generations [@tenaillon2016]. How many mutations distinguish these clones, and how sensitive are the counts to a minimum-depth filter? This report examines the reads, compares the filtered variant counts and checks their sensitivity to the minimum-depth filter.

## Data

```{python}
#| tags: [parameters]
max_reads = 10000
```

```{python}
#| label: setup
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from scripts.fastq_stats import quality_by_position, summarize

samples = pd.read_csv("metadata/samples.tsv", sep="\t", keep_default_na=False)
samples = samples.sort_values("generation")
fastq_files = samples["fastq_1"].tolist() + samples["fastq_2"].tolist()
generations = ", ".join(f"{g:,}" for g in samples["generation"])


def show_table(frame):
    # Emit a Markdown table so Quarto can render it in both HTML and PDF.
    rows = [frame.columns, ["---"] * len(frame.columns), *frame.itertuples(index=False, name=None)]
    display(Markdown("\n".join("| " + " | ".join(map(str, row)) + " |" for row in rows)))
```

The Data Carpentry teaching subset [@dc_data] contains paired reads from `{python} len(samples)` Ara-3 clones sampled at generations `{python} generations` (@tbl-samples). In the sample sheet, `None` is a recorded mutator status and `unknown` denotes an undetermined citrate-use phenotype.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-samples
#| tbl-cap: "LTEE clones in generation order. Sample identifiers are SRA runs."
show_table(samples[["sample", "strain", "generation", "mutator", "cit"]])
```

## Reads

@tbl-reads counts every record in each FASTQ file. The parameter limits the length, GC and base-quality summaries to the first `{python} f'{max_reads:,}'` reads per file. GC is the percentage of sampled bases that are G or C. Mean Q is the arithmetic mean of their Phred+33 scores. Each file identifier below omits the shared suffix `.trim.sub.fastq`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-reads
#| tbl-cap: "Full read counts and prefix summaries by run and mate (1 or 2)."
reads = pd.DataFrame([summarize(path, max_reads) for path in sorted(fastq_files)])
read_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "File": reads["file"].str.removesuffix(".trim.sub.fastq"),
    "Reads": reads["reads"].map("{:,}".format),
    "Mean length (bp)": reads["mean_length"].map("{:.1f}".format),
    "GC (%)": reads["gc_percent"].map("{:.1f}".format),
    "Mean Q": reads["mean_quality"].map("{:.1f}".format),
})
show_table(read_table)
```

```{python}
#| label: paired-counts
#| include: false
counts = reads.set_index("file")["reads"]
pairs = {}
for row in samples.itertuples(index=False):
    r1, r2 = (counts[Path(path).name] for path in (row.fastq_1, row.fastq_2))
    if r1 != r2:
        raise ValueError(f"Mates have different record counts for {row.sample}")
    pairs[row.sample] = r1
if len(set(pairs.values())) == 1:
    pair_text = f"{next(iter(pairs.values())):,} read pairs per clone"
else:
    pair_text = ", ".join(f"{count:,} read pairs for {run}" for run, count in pairs.items())
n_sampled = reads["reads"].clip(upper=max_reads)
mean_length = (reads["mean_length"] * n_sampled).sum() / n_sampled.sum()
```

The paired files contain `{python} pair_text`. Across the sampled reads, the mean length after trimming is `{python} f'{mean_length:.1f}'` bases.

## Quality along the read

```{python}
#| label: fig-quality
#| fig-cap: "Mean base quality by position in the sampled prefix of each FASTQ file. Colour identifies the clone and line style identifies the mate."
#| fig-alt: "Six quality profiles, one solid line for read 1 and one dashed line for read 2 of each clone. The horizontal axis is position from the start of a read; the vertical axis is mean Phred score among reads that reach that position. The text below gives the observed ranges at the two ends of the shared interval."
profiles = {}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.3))
for row, color in zip(samples.itertuples(index=False), ["#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73"]):
    for mate, path, style in [(1, row.fastq_1, "-"), (2, row.fastq_2, "--")]:
        q = quality_by_position(path, max_reads)
        profiles[(row.sample, mate)] = q
        ax.plot(q.index, q, color=color, linestyle=style, linewidth=1.4,
                label=f"{row.sample} R{mate}")
ax.set(xlabel="Position in read (bases)", ylabel="Mean Phred score")
ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
ax.legend(ncol=3, fontsize=8, frameon=False, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.16))
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: quality-ranges
#| include: false
last_shared = min(q.index[-1] for q in profiles.values())

def score_range(pos):
    values = [q.loc[pos] for q in profiles.values()]
    return f"{min(values):.1f}–{max(values):.1f}"
```

Across the six profiles in @fig-quality, the mean scores span `{python} score_range(1)` at base 1 and `{python} score_range(last_shared)` at base `{python} last_shared`, the last position shared by all profiles. Each point averages only reads long enough to contribute a base at that position.

## Variants

The workflow aligns paired reads to REL606, calls haploid variants with
bcftools and filters them with `vcfutils.pl varFilter`. Settings come from
`config/config.yaml`. The [MultiQC report](../results/qc/multiqc/multiqc_report.html)
contains the read-quality checks. Counts below describe variants called from
this teaching subset against the reference, rather than a complete catalogue
of mutations in each clone.

```{python}
#| label: setup-variants
import yaml

with open("config/config.yaml") as stream:
    config = yaml.safe_load(stream)


def count_variants(path):
    with open(path) as stream:
        return sum(1 for line in stream if line.strip() and not line.startswith("#"))


def percent_mapped(path):
    with open(path) as stream:
        for line in stream:
            if " mapped (" in line and "primary" not in line:
                return float(line.split("(", 1)[1].split("%", 1)[0])
    raise ValueError(f"Mapped percentage missing from {path}")


def stats_value(path, key):
    with open(path) as stream:
        for line in stream:
            fields = line.rstrip().split("\t")
            if len(fields) == 4 and fields[0] == "SN" and fields[2] == key:
                return int(fields[3])
    raise ValueError(f"{key} missing from {path}")


variants = samples[["sample", "generation", "mutator"]].copy()
variants["mapped_percent"] = [percent_mapped(f"results/stats/{s}.flagstat.txt") for s in variants["sample"]]
variants["variants"] = [count_variants(f"results/vcf/{s}_final_variants.vcf") for s in variants["sample"]]
variants["SNPs"] = [stats_value(f"results/stats/{s}.bcftools-stats.txt", "number of SNPs:") for s in variants["sample"]]
variants["indels"] = [stats_value(f"results/stats/{s}.bcftools-stats.txt", "number of indels:") for s in variants["sample"]]
```

At least `{python} f'{variants["mapped_percent"].min():.2f}'`% of alignment
records are mapped in each sample's flagstat summary. At minimum depth
`{python} config["min_depth"]`, the filtered variant count is
`{python} int(variants["variants"].iloc[0])` in the 5,000-generation clone and
`{python} int(variants["variants"].iloc[-1])` in the 50,000-generation clone
(@tbl-variants). The sample sheet records the latter as mutator `plus`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-variants
#| tbl-cap: "Mapping summaries and filtered variants at the configured minimum depth. SNP and indel counts come from bcftools stats."
variant_table = variants.copy()
variant_table["mapped_percent"] = variant_table["mapped_percent"].map("{:.2f}".format)
show_table(variant_table)
```

### Sensitivity to the minimum-depth filter

```{python}
#| label: setup-sensitivity
#| include: false
depths = sorted(config["sensitivity_depths"])
sens = pd.DataFrame([
    {"sample": row.sample, "generation": row.generation, "depth": depth,
     "variants": count_variants(f"results/sensitivity/{row.sample}_d{depth}.vcf")}
    for row in variants.itertuples(index=False) for depth in depths
])
table = sens.pivot(index=["sample", "generation"], columns="depth", values="variants").sort_index(level="generation")
ratios = table.iloc[-1] / table.iloc[-2]
if not (ratios > 1).all():
    raise ValueError("Revisit the decision: the final clone no longer has more calls at every threshold")
```

The workflow repeats the same filter at depths `{python} ', '.join(map(str, depths))`.
@fig-sensitivity and @tbl-sensitivity show the resulting counts, computed from
the VCF files at render time.

```{python}
#| label: fig-sensitivity
#| fig-cap: "Filtered variants against generation at each minimum depth. The y axis is logarithmic; colour identifies the threshold."
#| fig-alt: "Four lines compare variant counts across the three clones in generation order on a logarithmic y axis. Each line uses one minimum-depth threshold. The following table gives every value; the text states how the final two clones compare."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.2))
for depth, color in zip(depths, ["#86b6ef", "#5598e7", "#2a78d6", "#184f95"]):
    part = sens[sens["depth"] == depth].sort_values("generation")
    ax.plot(part["generation"], part["variants"], marker="o", color=color, label=f"min depth {depth}")
if (sens["variants"] > 0).all():
    ax.set_yscale("log")
generations_axis = sorted(sens["generation"].unique())
ax.set_xticks(generations_axis, [f"{g:,}" for g in generations_axis])
ax.set(xlabel="Generation", ylabel="Filtered variants")
ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Filtered variant counts at each minimum read depth."
show_table(table.reset_index())
```

**Decision.** Keep minimum depth `{python} config["min_depth"]` as the main
result for comparison with the Data Carpentry workflow, and report all tested
depths alongside it. Absolute counts change substantially with the threshold.
Across the tested depths, the 50,000-generation clone has
`{python} f'{ratios.min():.1f}'`–`{python} f'{ratios.max():.1f}'` times as many
calls as the 15,000-generation clone. This ordering is robust in these three
clones; the counts alone do not estimate a general mutation rate or establish
why the clones differ. The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.
